solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mr. O'Casey chopped up tree

indicators.note: something chopped up is cut into bits that can be put back together in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of the title and surname, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: The playwright Sean O'Casey is pictured felling a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The sycamore is a common broadleaf species, a type of maple, so it is an example of a tree.

clue.text: Bird in fight, then another fight

blocks.note: to spar is to box or fight
a row is a quarrel or fight

explanation.surface: A bird gets into one scrap after another.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small, common brown songbird.

clue.text: Dieter's concern, perhaps, consuming zero chocolate substitute

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so the outer word takes the other inside

blocks.note: a carb (carbohydrate) is what many dieters worry about
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A slimmer worries about eating chocolate that has no calories.
explanation.walkthrough: CARB takes in O: CAR(O)B. 'Perhaps' marks carbs as just one example of a dieter's concern.
explanation.definitionFit: Carob comes from the pods of a Mediterranean tree and is widely used in place of chocolate.

clue.text: His romances, rewritten for noblewoman

indicators.note: something rewritten has been recast, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A man's love stories are redrafted with an aristocratic heroine in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A marchioness is the wife or widow of a marquess, or a woman holding that rank herself.

clue.text: Charitable club go off on a railway

blocks.note: to rot is to decay, go off
taken as written
RY is short for railway; on just places it after

explanation.surface: Members of a charity outing head off on a train trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotary International is a worldwide service organisation of local clubs that raise money for good causes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotary is the name of an international network of service clubs known for charity work.

clue.text: Get away after outing Republican swindle

indicators.note: outing something means putting it out, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: scram is slang for leave quickly
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A fraudster flees once a Republican accomplice has been exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the R from SCRAM to leave SCAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme to cheat people, the same thing as a swindle.

clue.text: No good energy in fossil fuel, clot

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the word for the fuel

blocks.note: coal is a fossil fuel; it takes the other letters inside
N stands for no, as on a yes/no form
G is short for good
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An environmental slogan: fossil fuel has no good energy in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clot' is a verb here, not a noun; N for no is the mark on a yes/no form.
explanation.definitionFit: To congeal is to thicken and set from a liquid, which is what blood does when it clots.

clue.text: Particle very much accepted by blokes

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in by, so the intensifier goes inside the men

blocks.note: blokes is British slang for men
so means very, as in so glad

explanation.surface: A tiny thing is warmly welcomed by the lads.
explanation.definitionFit: A meson is a subatomic particle made of a quark and an antiquark.

clue.text: Artist backed retaining passion and support for clothes

indicators.note: going backwards means the artist's abbreviation is read from right to left
to retain is to hold on to, so one piece holds the other inside it

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist; turned round it reads AR
ire is anger, a strong passion

explanation.surface: A painter is said to have backed a passionate cause and offered support.
explanation.definitionFit: An airer is a frame or rack on which laundry is hung to dry, a support for clothes.

clue.text: News — it recalled activities, omitting nothing

indicators.note: recalled suggests calling something back, so the little word is read in the opposite direction
omitting means leaving out, so a letter goes from the word for activities

blocks.note: the word it, read backwards
doings are things being done, activities
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A news report recalls events while leaving nothing out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings is an old-fashioned word for news or information that is reported.

clue.text: Twice the helium and lithium unknown in molecule

blocks.note: double the means twice as much
He is the chemical symbol for helium
Li is the chemical symbol for lithium
x is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A chemist describes a molecule with two helium atoms, lithium and a mystery element.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the double helix is the twisted-ladder shape of the DNA molecule, so the whole molecule is named by its form.
explanation.definitionFit: DNA is commonly called the double helix after its two strands wound round each other.

clue.text: Flier cut back support for wing?

indicators.note: cutting a word short removes its final letter
back tells us to read what remains from right to left

blocks.note: a bird is a creature that flies

explanation.surface: A bird with clipped wings is pushed back and needs support.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRD loses its D, and BIR turned round is RIB. The question mark flags that a rib is one of the struts that supports an aircraft wing.
explanation.definitionFit: In aircraft construction, ribs are the internal struts that give a wing its shape and strength.

clue.text: Copper pursuing woman's slender and very strong

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the metal comes after the woman's word

blocks.note: the possessive pronoun for a woman
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
lean means thin, slender

explanation.surface: A police officer chases a woman who is slim but powerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman; here it is the chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Herculean, from the mythical strongman Hercules, describes enormous strength or effort.

clue.text: Detective's assistant initially has to miss coming events?

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows
missing something means going without it, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: the first letter of has
a what's on guide lists forthcoming events

explanation.surface: A sidekick, it seems, is bound to miss what lies ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the H out of WHAT'S ON. Dr Watson is Sherlock Holmes's companion and chronicler.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr John Watson is the friend and helper of the fictional detective Sherlock Holmes.

clue.text: Biting insect not half minor in producing irritations

indicators.note: not half means half is missing, so only part of the word for minor is used

blocks.note: a tick is a blood-sucking parasite
lesser means smaller, minor

explanation.surface: A small insect bite causing only minor itching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' here means only half the word is kept, its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickles are ticklish sensations, mild irritations such as a tickle in the throat.

clue.text: Look, engaging in a lot of tricks in skiing event

indicators.note: engaging in means getting inside, so the short word sits within the longer one

blocks.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
in bridge, a slam is winning all or all but one of the tricks

explanation.surface: A skier performs plenty of stunts during a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricks' suggests stunts, but here it is the card-game sense from bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Slalom is an alpine ski race in which competitors zigzag between gates on a downhill course.

clue.text: Slander linked to apartment, riverside feature

blocks.note: to sling mud is to slander, so mud is defamation
flat is the British word for an apartment

explanation.surface: Defamatory claims are tied to a flat with a river view.
explanation.definitionFit: A mudflat is a stretch of muddy land left exposed at low tide along an estuary or river.

clue.text: Academic supporting standard act of clemency

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means sitting beneath, so the academic goes below

blocks.note: par is the normal or standard level
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A university lecturer backs the usual practice of showing mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pardon is an official forgiveness of a crime, a merciful act by those in authority.

clue.text: I will leave city chapel, upset, pedalling away here?

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that letter goes from the fodder
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letter taken out
the fodder, before one letter leaves

explanation.surface: Someone, cross about a city chapel, decides to cycle off.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the I from CITY CHAPEL and rearrange the nine letters left. The question mark marks the definition as playful: a cycle path is where you pedal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle path is a track set aside for bicycles, the place where riders pedal along.

clue.text: Pain in the neck caught atop haystack?

indicators.note: atop puts this letter above the next part in a down answer

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a rick is a stack of hay

explanation.surface: Someone hurt their neck after being trapped on top of a haystack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pain in the neck' usually means a nuisance; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A crick is a painful stiffness, especially of the neck or back, a literal pain in the neck.

clue.text: Accompanied by genetic material, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is back to front, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: DNA carries genetic information

explanation.surface: Someone has their genome examined and thinks about it afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction joins one thing to another, so 'X and Y' means X accompanied by Y.

clue.text: Reason gendarmes initially seen in a street in Paris

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
seen in means appearing inside, so that letter goes within the street

blocks.note: taken as written
rue is French for street
the first letter of gendarmes

explanation.surface: Reasoning that French police were spotted on a Paris street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reason' is a verb here: to reason a case is to make it.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue is to give reasons in support of a view, so reason and argue are synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: Mishandled American editor after one pair of lines

indicators.note: after places the American editor letters behind the preceding pieces

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
L is lines; two of them
US is short for American
ed. is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An American editor botched a couple of lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-used means treated badly or unfairly, the same as mishandled.

clue.text: Cricket side almost completely following the rules

indicators.note: almost means not quite, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: the leg side is one half of a cricket field, the batter's legward side
all means wholly, completely

explanation.surface: A cricket team plays almost entirely within the laws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cricket side' looks like a team; it is the leg side, also called on side, of the field. ALL loses its last L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something legal is permitted by law, so it is in line with the rules.

clue.text: Gentle contact is accepted by King and son

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in by, so the short word goes inside the others

blocks.note: K is king in chess notation
taken as written
S is short for son

explanation.surface: A monarch and his son greet each other lightly.
explanation.walkthrough: K and S hold IS: K(IS)S. In snooker a kiss is a light touch between balls.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss is a light touch of the lips, and more generally any brief, gentle contact.

clue.text: One subsequently coming round for each amateur?

indicators.note: coming round means surrounding, so this word wraps another

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
next means afterwards
per means for each

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about who comes along for each novice.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits an amateur need not be unskilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexpert means lacking skill, which is how an amateur may be, though not always.
